statements.text: Midpoint C of A(1, 2) and B(5, 6) is found by averaging coordinates: C((1+5)/2, (2+6)/2), i.e. C(3, 4). Formula: $C\left(\frac{1+5}{2}, \frac{2+6}{2}\right)=C(3, 4)$

If A(x1, y1), B(x2, y2), M(x, y) where M is the midpoint of AB, then triangles BEM and MDA are congruent, so AD = ME. Hence x − x1 = x2 − x, so 2x = x1 + x2, x = (x1+x2)/2. Similarly MD = BE gives y − y1 = y2 − y, so 2y = y1 + y2, y = (y1+y2)/2. So M((x1+x2)/2, (y1+y2)/2). Formula: $M\left(\frac{x_1+x_2}{2}, \frac{y_1+y_2}{2}\right)$
